solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Find exact place that could give you a sharp prick

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to locate something precisely

definitions.text: that could give you a sharp prick
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read as two words: the sharp tip of a pin

explanation.surface: A rather painful way of finding where something is.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads the answer split in two, as the tip of a pin.
explanation.definitionFit: To pinpoint is a verb for locating something with complete precision.

clue.text: Engineers finished meal

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
something finished is over and past

explanation.surface: The engineers have stopped work and eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: A repast is a formal or literary word for a meal.

clue.text: Bad weather only half rare during autumn

indicators.note: only half of the word is kept, here its front portion

parts.note: the first two of its four letters
during a time is in it
fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: Unpleasant weather in autumn is only half as rare as you might hope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'During' is not a placing instruction here: it simply gives IN, which stands between the half of rare and the season.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain is what most people mean by bad weather, and rainfall is a fall of it.

clue.text: A bit of cloud in view is pleasant

indicators.note: the answer sits in the run of words that follows

parts.note: the end of view, the whole of is and the start of pleasant

explanation.surface: A small cloud makes the view pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: A wisp is a thin, small streak, as of cloud or smoke.

clue.text: I have no suntan: spit!

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am, read as I have got to
someone without a tan is pale

explanation.surface: Someone complains that they have no tan and spits in disgust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spit' looks like a noun or an angry outburst; it is the verb, to skewer meat on a spit.
explanation.definitionFit: To spit meat is to run it through with a skewer, which is to impale it.

clue.text: Came struggling to make summit

indicators.note: struggling suggests thrashing about, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A climber arrived, toiling, to reach the top of the mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: The acme is the highest point or peak of something.

clue.text: Extra starters from waiter in diner eventually

indicators.note: starters are the opening course, so take the opening of each word

parts.note: first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: In a diner, the waiter eventually brings the starters and some extra.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a wide is a ball bowled out of the batsman's reach, and it counts as an extra run.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide is one of the extras in cricket, runs not scored off the bat.

clue.text: Little followed by lots is unreasonable

parts.note: a little is a bit
lots is much

explanation.surface: Having a small amount and then a lot more is excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling something a bit much is an idiom for saying it goes too far.

clue.text: Rick, resident originally in a warmer country

parts.note: a European country warmer than Britain

indicators.note: originally points to the very start of the word

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: Rick, who lives in a sunny country, is described.
explanation.walkthrough: Rick looks like a man's name; it is a verb meaning to wrench a joint.
explanation.definitionFit: To rick a joint is to strain or twist it, a synonym of sprain.

clue.text: Soft bed for sportsman

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical marking for soft
a bed is a layer, as of rock

explanation.surface: A soft mattress for an athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is someone who takes part in a sport or game.

clue.text: Outfit including line in national dress

indicators.note: one word takes the other inside it

parts.note: kit is a set of clothes or gear
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A costume that includes something lined, worn as a country's dress.
explanation.definitionFit: The kilt is part of Scotland's traditional national costume.

clue.text: A large painting done out of doors

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for large
a fresco is a painting on wet plaster

explanation.surface: A big painting was made outside.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the painting was done outdoors; in fact 'done out of doors' is all definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Al fresco is Italian for in the fresh air, describing things done outside.

clue.text: Tidy file? Somehow that's showing devotion

indicators.note: somehow means in some unknown way, so the letters are rearranged in an unspecified manner

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A neat filing system shows how devoted its keeper is.
explanation.definitionFit: Fidelity is faithful loyalty, the constancy of someone devoted.

clue.text: Annoyed to travel regularly on such a tyre?

parts.note: annoyed is cross
a ferry or bus plies a route when it travels it regularly

explanation.surface: A motorist is irritated to drive the same route on this kind of tyre.
explanation.walkthrough: A cross-ply tyre has its cord layers running diagonally across one another.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross-ply is a type of tyre construction, older than radial-ply.

clue.text: Astonished from the off: was in front!

parts.note: the off is the start of a race
to lead is to be in front

explanation.surface: Surprised to have been leading a race right from the beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: Startled means taken aback by sudden surprise or alarm.

clue.text: Artist is home for a little fruit

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician
taken as written
at home is in

explanation.surface: A painter stays in, with a bit of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A raisin is a dried grape, a small piece of fruit.

clue.text: Cut round circular figure to make a coil

parts.note: to lop is to cut off
the letter O is circular in shape

explanation.surface: Instructions for cutting round a circle to form a spiral.
explanation.definitionFit: A loop is a curve of rope or wire that turns back on itself, like one turn of a coil.

clue.text: Identify centre of loch, not in time to go round

parts.note: not punctual is late

indicators.note: centre of asks for the middle letters only

parts.note: its two middle letters

explanation.surface: Find the middle of a Scottish lake before time runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: A loch is a Scottish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: To locate something is to find or identify where it is.

clue.text: Female telling stories in a plane?

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female
telling stories is a gentle way of saying telling lies

explanation.surface: A woman spins tales while on a flight.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in a plane is flying; the question mark flags the definition by example.

clue.text: Strong desire of lieutenant to tour America

indicators.note: touring a place means travelling all round it

parts.note: Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant
the US is America

explanation.surface: An officer longs to travel around the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Lust is intense craving, a powerful desire.

clue.text: Rudely take lighter, shortly given up

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top
shortly means cut short, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a lighter is a flat-bottomed barge used to load ships

explanation.surface: Someone snatches a cigarette lighter that was soon surrendered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lighter' looks like the thing for lighting cigarettes; here it is the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To grab is to seize something roughly or without asking.

clue.text: Place and time for crop pest

parts.note: locus is Latin for place
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Setting a place and time to deal with a pest in the crops.
explanation.definitionFit: Locusts are grasshoppers that swarm and devour crops.

clue.text: Candidate is poisonous creature, I storm angrily

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake
taken as written
to rant is to rage loudly

explanation.surface: A poisonous applicant for a job rages and storms about.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspirant is someone who aspires to a post, a candidate for it.

clue.text: Related to lord

parts.note: taken as written
Ld is the abbreviation for lord

explanation.walkthrough: 'Related' looks like family ties; it is the past tense of relate, to tell.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate a story is to recount it, so related means narrated.
